title: If-Then, But Not Then-If
body: The claim was: if {antecedent}, then {consequent}. True. But then someone argued: so if {consequent}, then {antecedent}. That's the converse fallacy. {antecedent} is sufficient for {consequent}, but {consequent} doesn't prove {antecedent}. The correct contrapositive is: if not {consequent}, then not {antecedent}.
